settings.description: The most connectors one person may have: MCP servers, on this machine or remote, whose tools a chat may use.
How long Keystone waits for a connector's server to start a session and list its tools. A command that is slow to start, such as one fetched by a package runner the first time, may need longer.
How long a session with a connector's server is kept open after its last call. A local command is stopped then, and started again by the next call.
The most tools Keystone takes from one connector. A server that lists more has the rest left out.
The most bytes of one message Keystone reads from a connector's server. A larger message is refused. agents.tool_result_max_chars still cuts every result.
The most characters of the one line a connector's tool is offered with before its full definition is loaded with load_tools.
The most tools one call of load_tools may load.
How long Keystone waits before it tries again to reach a connector that has never listed its tools and could not be reached when a chat asked for tools.

The id of the Google OAuth client this person's Gmail and Calendar connectors sign in with, from the Google Cloud console. Empty means Google is not set up for them. The client's secret is stored in their vault as google.client_secret, never here.

The address Google sends the browser back to after this person signs in, as registered on the OAuth client, such as https://keystone.example/settings/connectors/google. Empty means the address of the page Connect Google was pressed on, with /settings/connectors/google.
Google's sign-in page, where Connect Google sends the browser.
Google's token address, where Keystone trades a sign-in's code for tokens and gets new access tokens.
Google's address for revoking a sign-in, used when a person disconnects Google.
The Gmail API, up to and not including /users.
The Google Calendar API, up to and not including /calendars.
How long one call to Google may take, its sign-in included.
How long a Google sign-in may take from Connect Google to the browser's return. A sign-in that takes longer is refused, and the person connects again.
The most messages one Gmail search, or events one calendar list, returns. From 1 to 100.
How long a tool call waits for your approval before it is answered as not run. The turn waits with it, and goes on when you answer. From 1s to 720h.
Whether a chat turn offers the model tools. When it is off no tool is offered, and a tool a model asks for anyway is answered with a refusal.
How long one tool may run in a turn. A tool that runs longer is stopped, and the model is told it gave no result.
The most characters of one tool's result that are kept and sent back to the model. A longer result is cut, with a line that says so. Zero keeps every result whole.

settings.default: Keystone stopped here, because this reply reached the most steps one turn may take. Send another message to carry on from this point.
settings.description: What a reply ends with when a turn reaches chats.turn_max_steps while the model is still asking for tools. The person reads it in the chat, and the model reads it in later turns.
The most messages the read_chat tool returns from one chat. A longer chat comes back as its last messages.
The address web_search sends its searches to: Tavily's search API. The person's own key, stored as provider.tavily, goes with each search.
Tavily's search depth. A basic search costs one Tavily credit and an advanced one two.
How many results web_search returns when the model does not ask for a number.
The most results one web search may return, whatever number the model asks for. At most 20.
The most characters of each search result's text that the model reads.
How long one web search may take before it is given up, and the model is told it has no results.
The most bytes of a search provider's answer that are read. A larger answer is not used.
How long web_fetch may take to read one page, redirects included.
The most bytes of one page web_fetch reads. A longer page is read as far as this, and the model is told so.
The most characters of a page's readable text that web_fetch returns. A longer text is cut, with a line that says so.
The most redirects web_fetch follows for one page. Each one is checked like the first address: only public addresses are read.

The most one background task may spend, in US dollars, on models that are not local. A call that could take the task past it is not sent: the task goes on with a local model if your fallback chain has one, and otherwise stops and says so. The monthly cap still applies to every call.

The most rounds one background task may take. A round is one turn of its chat, of up to chats.turn_max_steps model calls; a round that ends at its step limit, or that a restart cut short, is followed by another until this many have run.
The most background tasks one person may have waiting or running at once. Starting another is refused until one ends.

settings.default: Carry on with the task from where you stopped. When it is finished, give the result in full: it is what the person will read.
settings.description: The message a background task's next round is sent with when the round before it reached the step limit. The model reads it.

settings.default: Keystone was restarted while you were working on this task, and your last step was cut short. Carry on from where you stopped: check what was done before you do anything again. When it is finished, give the result in full.
settings.description: The message a background task's next round is sent with when a restart of Keystone cut the round before it short. The model reads it.
